headline: An unidentified actor took root on unpatched Check Point gateways and wiped VMware ESXi files at Israeli organizations, while the FBI warned that the open-source ARTEX framework now drives intrusions from first targeting to privileged access in under three hours.

emerging_trends.text: The FBI's flash alert on ARTEX, which it says carries some intrusions from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours, landed the same day Cisco Talos surveyed the wider field of AI penetration-testing platforms and OpenAI opened early access to its own agent-driven red team, putting attackers and defenders on the same tooling.
emerging_trends.topic_title: FBI Flash Alert Puts ARTEX Intrusions Under Three Hours

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep working the software that manages other people's computers, exploiting N-central zero-days within hours of a published proof of concept and riding the SCKit toolkit through ScreenConnect into technician sessions, which turns one vendor flaw into reach across every customer network.

topics.title: Check Point Gateways Fall to PHP2Shell and a Gaia OS Bug
topics.latest_developments: CISA added CVE-2026-123039, the Check Point privilege escalation flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 13, 2026, alongside CVE-2026-114713 in UnrealIRCd, hours after Check Point shipped emergency hotfixes for the high-severity bug attackers have exploited since late October to take root and hold persistence; Check Point detailed a campaign that started October 30, 2026 against Israeli organizations, in which an unidentified actor entered unpatched Security Gateways through the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, escalated to root with CVE-2026-123039, a previously unreported local privilege escalation in Gaia OS, installed a backdoor named TSGA, and ran data-wiping malware against connected VMware ESXi hosts, with a wider wave following; Citrix separately closed 10 critical NetScaler vulnerabilities that drive unexpected behavior and denial of service.
topics.summary: Check Point Security Gateways sit at the perimeter of enterprise networks and route all traffic through Gaia OS. Administrators should install the hotfixes immediately, hunt for TSGA, and check ESXi datastores for deleted files.

topics.title: FBI Flash Alert Puts ARTEX Intrusions Under Three Hours
topics.latest_developments: The FBI issued a flash alert on November 13, 2026 warning that ARTEX, the open-source agentic hacking framework, cuts the work of chaining attack techniques so far that some intrusions run from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours; Cisco Talos published its own survey of AI-enabled penetration testing and red team platforms the same day, mapping how they automate reconnaissance, vulnerability testing, and follow-on actions and lower the skill a break-in demands; and OpenAI opened early access to Daybreak Red Team, which runs coordinated agents against web applications and verifies fixes, paired with Defense Factory, which investigates findings and prepares patches.
topics.summary: ARTEX and similar frameworks let one operator run a complete intrusion chain at machine speed against any exposed application. Defenders should plan for hours between first contact and privileged access, and tune detection toward fast automated reconnaissance and credential attacks.

topics.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Enters a Second Day
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft brought Microsoft 365 back on November 13, 2026 after roughly 24 hours and said a bad update crashed its servers around the world, ruling out a cyberattack and ruling out AI, after telling customers through the morning that it was taking a measured approach to identify and repair affected infrastructure; Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, and Copilot returned for business and enterprise customers, and Wired counted businesses, schools, hospitals, and governments learning the cost of running their work on one company's systems.
topics.summary: The failure hit the mail, meeting, and assistant services that most large companies run their day on, and it left staff whose jobs consist of email unable to send any. Operations teams should keep an out-of-band communication channel ready and watch for phishing that impersonates outage notices.

topics.title: Operation TorNado Arrests 354 Dark Web Traders
topics.latest_developments: Europol and police in 14 countries arrested 354 dark web vendors and buyers in Operation TorNado, which ran from May 2025 to October 2026 and worked backward from five marketplaces already taken offline—Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom, and Tor2Door—as well as forums and single-vendor shops; investigators put this week's Operation Endgame round at 235 servers and 257 domains seized behind Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC, with 6.4 million stolen logins recovered from more than 40,000 victims, according to Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office; and Justice Department officials briefed reporters on November 13, 2026 that Gootloader served at least 44 ransomware attacks costing $29 million since 2018.
topics.summary: Both operations show that a marketplace or botnet takedown leaves a usable evidence trail against the people who traded on it. Organizations should assume credentials harvested by StealC and Gootloader circulate now and force resets on accounts appearing in the recovered sets.

topics.title: North Korea Runs Fake Zoom Calls and Fake Engineers
topics.latest_developments: The FBI put the FaceStealer scheme at more than $400 million in cryptocurrency stolen over 18 months, said it has seized more than 900 webcam recordings the operators replay to make fake Zoom and Microsoft Teams calls look real, and warned cryptocurrency and web3 employees plus open-source maintainers on November 12, 2026; Material Security reported the same week that it tracked 27 fabricated North Korean job-seeker personas through the hiring pipelines of organizations it monitors all the way to onboarding over one year, and that one company a persona reached in the past month kept roughly 277,000 files holding Social Security numbers open to everyone in the company or to anyone with a public link; and Dark Reading reported that the crew behind the $1.2 billion Binance theft worked a known weakness and absent controls, with attacker-deployed sweeper contracts blunting the exchange's damage limits.
topics.summary: North Korean operators infect a target during a video call that shows stolen footage of earlier victims, then drain wallets, and they also apply for remote engineering jobs under invented identities. Companies hiring remote engineers should verify identity documents against live video and lock down company-wide file sharing before onboarding anyone.

topics.title: N-able Restricts N-central as Agent2Shell Spreads
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published the SCKit attack chain on November 13, 2026, detailing how the toolkit abuses ConnectWise ScreenConnect to plant unauthorized remote access and work its way into technician sessions, and shipped Microsoft Defender XDR hunting queries and mitigations; N-able said on Thursday, November 12, 2026 that it is restricting certain N-central features and integrations while remediation continues, after a researcher published a second flaw set named Agent2Shell alongside 4EverAble2Shell, the zero-day that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker run code as root and that attackers turned on within hours of the proof of concept, planting cryptocurrency miners on at least 21 servers, 19 of them running the company's newest hotfix.
topics.summary: N-central manages endpoints for managed service providers, so one compromised server reaches every customer network it touches. Operators should apply the hotfixes, keep the Legacy API off and off the public internet, and hunt for miners and new root accounts.

topics.title: Ransomware Strands a Belarusian Cloud as Apify Loses Data
topics.latest_developments: Osaka, Japan's third-largest city, told its 2.8 million residents on November 13, 2026 to treat email purporting to come from the city government with suspicion after a breach of its email system exposed data on 1 million people, the newest of dozens of cyber incidents Japan has absorbed this autumn; ActiveCloud, the Belarusian cloud provider, said hackers breached its systems and encrypted parts of its cloud infrastructure, cutting customers off from key services for several days; Apify, the web scraping company, confirmed the same day that an intruder reached customer accounts and took personal information and stored data; and TSMC, the Taiwanese chipmaker, confirmed that stolen employee data matched records held in the system services of a cloud service provider it uses and said no TSMC system fell.
topics.summary: A single hosting or data-platform compromise takes every tenant's service and stored secrets with it. Companies should inventory which suppliers hold their credentials and data, demand breach notification terms, and rehearse operating without each one.

topics.title: November Windows Updates Break Printing and Activation
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft confirmed on November 13, 2026 that the November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fail Windows activation and licensing with 0x80041008 errors, and warned earlier in the week that the same updates may break printing of documents carrying complex formatting; researchers meanwhile spelled out the mechanism of SignDrop, the unpatched Windows zero-day exploit that Abdelhamid Naceri, who goes by Nightmare Eclipse, published this week in frustration with Microsoft, which abuses the Common Log File System driver and Windows Defender to create arbitrary files in the antimalware process's context and hand a local user SYSTEM rights.
topics.summary: The November release closed more than 1,200 flaws, including the exploited Outlook zero-day CVE-2026-124194, so skipping it carries real risk. Administrators should stage the rollout, keep a licensing and printing rollback plan ready, and track Microsoft's release health notes for the fixes.

topics.title: SilentAir Intercepts SMS Codes Inside Asian Carriers
topics.latest_developments: Enea, the Stockholm telecommunications and cybersecurity software company, named a new espionage group SilentAir this week, reporting that it hijacks network nodes inside Asian mobile operators to intercept the calls and text messages of selected people, most of them Taiwanese subscribers, and that its attack sources trace to at least six Asian countries; Enea assesses with high confidence that a state runs it.
topics.summary: SilentAir reads traffic from inside carrier networks, which hands it the one-time codes that SMS two-factor authentication delivers. Any organization protecting accounts with text-message codes should move high-value users to hardware keys or app-based authentication.

topics.title: Germany Grants Spies Hacking Powers as Attackers Hit a Drone Maker
topics.latest_developments: The Bundestag passed a bill on November 13, 2026 by 308 votes to 190, with 71 abstentions, that hands German intelligence agencies hacking and sabotage powers, the largest rewrite of the country's spy laws since the war and the product of a draft Chancellor Friedrich Merz's cabinet approved months earlier; the same day, Quantum Systems, the German defense technology company whose aircraft fly for the German military, confirmed it caught an incident in late October that formed part of an active cyberattack by what it called hostile actors, and the attack disrupted military drone operations.
topics.summary: Germany now lets its intelligence services break into systems and conduct sabotage, a step its parliament debated for months, while its drone supply chain absorbs an active attack. Defense suppliers and their subcontractors should expect state-level targeting and verify that they detect intrusions in production and flight-operations systems.

business_politics.title: A Microsoft Outage Takes Down Outlook and Teams Worldwide
business_politics.latest_developments: The failure ran 19 hours, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday night, November 13, and Microsoft reported "continued recovery progress" while warning that intermittent access and delayed email delivery may persist; the German government said it anticipates "a very big impact" on the country's economy.
business_politics.summary: The outage knocked out the software that large organizations run their daily operations on, including email, messaging, and the Copilot assistant, and it reached banks, governments, county sheriffs, and pharmacies across continents. Microsoft attributes the fault to its own systems and says no malicious or cyber activity caused it, which puts the concentration risk of a single cloud and productivity vendor in front of every operations and continuity desk.

events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette took readers Friday, November 13, through a Cranberry house decorated for the Symphony Splendor Holiday House Tour, the Pittsburgh Symphony benefit that opens homes in the North Hills to ticket holders.
events.summary: The tour sends visitors through private houses dressed for the holidays, and the proceeds support the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra. NEXTpittsburgh counts it among six winter house tours running across the greater Pittsburgh region this season.

events.title: Encore Players Put Performers Over 55 Onstage
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, November 13, on Encore Players, a new McCandless theater group that casts only performers aged 55 and up.
events.summary: The company gives older actors in the North Hills a stage of their own, and its organizers summed up the premise this way: "Creativity doesn't have an expiration date."

sources.title: Ages 55 and up are in the spotlight at new McCandless theater group: 'Creativity doesn't have an expiration date'

around_teams.title: Hurleman Enters the Receiver Conversation
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Steelers desk asked Friday, November 13, whether Max Hurleman, the receiver nicknamed "White Chocolate," gets into the mix as Pittsburgh searches for answers at wide receiver.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers let the November 10 trade deadline pass without a deal, which leaves DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. to carry a passing game that Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy themselves call a work in progress two days before the Sunday night game at Cincinnati.

sources.title: As the Steelers search for answers at wide receiver, could 'White Chocolate' get in the mix?

around_teams.title: Tomlin Explains Why He Walked Away
around_teams.latest_developments: Not Just Football with Cam Heyward posted a video Friday, November 13, at noon Eastern in which Mike Tomlin explains why he really left the Steelers, and cut a clip the same morning in which the hosts say the Minecraft narrative that grew up around Tomlin "went a little overboard."
around_teams.summary: Tomlin stepped down as Steelers head coach and now works for NBC, and he gave Heyward and co-host Hayden a two-part sit-down that ran November 10 and November 12. The show keeps pulling clips from it, including Tomlin's account of the practice tape behind James Harrison's pick-six in Super Bowl XLIII.

around_teams.title: The Playoff Question Follows Pittsburgh to Cincinnati
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette asked Friday, November 13, why the Steelers keep winning regular-season showdowns and cannot win a playoff game, two days before the Sunday night trip to Cincinnati.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh plays the Cincinnati Bengals Sunday, November 15, at 8:20 p.m. Eastern on NBC, carrying a four-game winning streak and a defense the paper has described as potentially historic. The record in January games hangs over a team built on that defense and a 43-year-old quarterback in Aaron Rodgers.

sources.title: Why are the Steelers so good in regular-season showdowns yet can't win a playoff game?

around_teams.title: The Pirates Zero In on One Need
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Pirates desk reported Friday, November 13, that Pittsburgh stays open-minded about ways to improve this winter and has settled on one clear need as the offseason market opens.
around_teams.summary: General manager Ben Cherington came out of Major League Baseball's general managers meetings describing the payroll and roster flexibility to add, with Tampa Bay Rays infielder Brandon Lowe among the names in play, and the club has acknowledged a significant gap between itself and the Milwaukee Brewers and the Rays.

sources.title: The Pirates are open-minded about improving, but they have zeroed in on one clear need

around_teams.title: The Steelers Call the Passing Game a Work in Progress
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, November 13, that Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy describe the Steelers passing game as a "work in progress" and laid out how they intend to fix it, two days before the game at Cincinnati.
around_teams.summary: Rodgers met the media Wednesday, November 11, in his first session after the bye and the trade deadline, and the Steelers posted the full press conference. The passing offense remains the soft spot on a team riding its defense into a Sunday night meeting with the Bengals for the AFC North lead.

around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted Thursday's press conference, November 12, with Cameron Heyward, Jamel Dean, DK Metcalf, Brock Hoffman, and Germie Bernard, and SNR Drive spent the same afternoon on the Week 10 stats packet.
around_teams.summary: Hosts Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler worked through Bill Barnwell's midseason awards and the numbers heading into Cincinnati, and took a call from Mike DeFabo of The Athletic. team_usa.title: The U.S. Routs Denmark and Draws Finland
team_usa.latest_developments: The defending champion United States crushed host Denmark 14-0 Friday, November 13, to reach the semifinals of the women's ice hockey world championship, where it meets Finland.
team_usa.summary: The Americans went through the tournament without a loss, running up Hilary Knight's hat trick against the Czech Republic, Caroline Harvey's three goals against Austria, and a 5-0 shutout of Germany along the way. Canada beat Czechia 3-2 the same day to take the other semifinal place.

team_usa.title: Naeher Retires After 16 Years
team_usa.latest_developments: Alyssa Naeher announced her retirement from professional soccer Friday, November 13, closing a 16-year career.
team_usa.summary: Naeher kept goal for the Chicago Stars of the National Women's Soccer League and for the United States women's national team, and ESPN calls her a legend of both. Her exit leaves the next United States coaching staff to settle a goalkeeping depth chart before the Concacaf W Championship.

sources.title: USWNT, NWSL legend Alyssa Naeher announces retirement after 16-year career

team_usa.title: Girma's Fitness Clouds the W Championship
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Friday, November 13, that United States defender Naomi Girma remains a fitness concern for the Concacaf W Championship later this month, a tournament that doubles as a World Cup decider.
team_usa.summary: Girma, who plays for Chelsea in England, has carried fitness problems through the season, and she anchors the United States women's national team back line. Her availability shapes how the Americans line up in the matches that settle their World Cup qualification.

sources.title: USWNT's Girma in doubt for World Cup decider amid ongoing fitness concerns

team_usa.title: Pochettino Agrees to Manage Manchester United
team_usa.latest_developments: Manchester United confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as its head coach Friday, November 13, and U.S. Soccer said he leaves the United States men's national team on November 17, with Steve Cherundolo running the December camp on an interim basis; a tearful Pochettino called the departure the toughest decision of his career.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino replaces Michael Carrick, whom Manchester United sacked Thursday, November 12, with the team in the relegation zone. ESPN's reckoning of his United States tenure describes real highs shadowed by a mercenary feel and an eye on a return to Europe, and ESPN's transfer reporting has United looking at two of his American internationals, AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun and defender Alex Freeman.

team_usa.title: Rapinoe, Altidore, and Ertz Enter the Hall of Fame
team_usa.latest_developments: The National Soccer Hall of Fame elected Megan Rapinoe, Jozy Altidore, and Julie Ertz on Thursday, November 12, all on the first ballot, and David Beckham also won election.
team_usa.summary: Rapinoe and Ertz anchored the United States women's national teams that won the 2015 and 2019 World Cups, and Altidore scored 42 goals for the men's national team across more than a decade. The class puts three recently retired American internationals into the hall in a single vote.
